880: They strolled in like they owned the place, nodded at me kindly, and I nearly thanked them for visiting.
881: They walked past me so confidently I assumed they worked here, and I held the door for them.
882: They greeted me by a name that isn't mine, and I was too polite to correct such a fine person.
883: They admired my uniform, asked where I got it, and treated the whole visit like a grand tour.
884: They complimented me on how calm I keep the lobby, and the lobby has not been calm since.
885: They asked me to guard their coat, and I did, because they asked so importantly.
886: They wished me a good day twice, tipped their hat, and I only later wondered why they tipped it.
887: They strolled through the lobby waving at customers as if they had personally invited each one.
888: They asked me the safest place to keep something valuable, and I helpfully pointed the way.
889: They shook my hand, thanked me for my service, and I stood a little taller for an hour.
890: They walked in slowly enough for everyone to admire them, which is exactly what everyone did.
891: Nothing about them alarmed me, which I now understand was rather the whole point.
892: They asked if the vault was as impressive as people said, and I proudly assured them it was.
893: They treated my post like a welcome desk and asked me to announce their arrival.
894: They complimented how well I guard the door, then asked which doors I guard the least.
895: They moved through the bank like it was theirs, and for a few minutes I quite believed it.
896: They paused to fix their collar in the polished doors, as if the bank existed to reflect them.
897: They told me to relax, that everything was under control, and I relaxed, which I now regret.
898: They asked whether I ever leave my post, purely out of friendly conversation, they assured me.
899: They saluted me on the way out with such flair that I saluted back before I thought about it.
900: They withdrew a fortune in our largest bills and pushed one back across as a gift to me.
901: They asked for the money in the biggest notes we had, then complained the stack was too thin.
902: They took an enormous sum and did not count a single bill, trusting me with a grand little wave.
903: They requested so much cash I had to fetch more, and they waited tapping the counter like royalty.
904: They tipped me for handing over their own money, and the tip was more than I earn in a week.
905: They asked for the fortune to be wrapped nicely, as though it were a present to themselves.
906: They wanted only the crispest bills, and sent back any that had ever been folded.
907: They withdrew everything at once, tucked it away without looking, and thanked me like I'd been generous.
908: They asked which bills were worth the most, then asked for a great many of only those.
909: They slid a tip under the window so large I nearly returned it as a mistake.
910: They counted nothing, questioned nothing, and left as if money were simply an inconvenience.
911: They asked me to double the withdrawal for no reason except that a bigger number pleased them.
912: They wanted the money in a single grand bundle, not several tidy ones, for the drama of it.
913: They tipped me, tipped the customer behind them, and would have tipped the wall if it had a hand.
914: They took a small mountain of cash and asked, quite seriously, whether we had anything grander.
915: They withdrew a fortune and left the receipt behind, saying they never keep track of such trifles.
916: They asked for the largest bills, held one up to the light, and admired it like a portrait.
917: They took the full sum without counting and tipped me handsomely for my honesty, which they had not once checked.
918: They had me read the balance aloud, then asked me to read it again, slowly, so they could savor it.
919: They left a tip on the counter and a wink, and both were far too large for a simple withdrawal.
